answer: Sodium hydroxide (labelled NaOH (base)) is in the burette; the flask holds acid with a few drops of phenolphthalein (labelled acid + phenolphthalein).

Pink flashes where each drop lands, then fades as you swirl, so early on you can add the base quickly. (Note: on screen the flash was drawn as a yellow/gold patch, not pink, so the picture did not match the word.)
When the pink starts to linger instead of fading.
A faint pink that lasts thirty seconds. (On screen the whole liquid turned a pale olive/yellowish tint rather than pink.)
Stop adding base and read the volume on the burette; the clip showed a reading of 22.40 mL.
A pale, grey-blue, nearly colourless liquid (drawn as a light translucent fill).
A circular timer counting up from 0 s to 30 s, next to the label 'must last 30 s'.
Above: the burette hangs directly over the flask and drips down into it.
